headline_item.title_zh: 纳斯达克100指数单周跌逾10%创六年新低
headline_item.title_en: US tech stocks plunge into bear market in worst week since Covid-19 crisis
headline_item.event_summary_zh: 纳斯达克100指数周五收跌5.6%，全周累计跌幅达10.4%，创下自2018年以来的最差周度表现
headline_item.event_summary_en: The Nasdaq 100 index fell 5.6% on Friday, bringing the total weekly decline to 10.4%, marking its worst weekly performance in over six years. This volatility was driven by significant sell-offs in leading AI infrastructure and model firms like NVIDIA and Anthropic, reflecting a shift in investor sentiment regarding the translation of heavy AI capital expenditures into sustainable corporate earnings.
core_facts_zh: 【核心事件】纳斯达克100指数成分股（含英伟达、Anthropic）在美国资本市场交易环境：周五单日跌幅5.6%，全周累计跌幅10.4%
【起因与机理】AI投资回报率预期下滑引发的市场估值重估
【关键数据与实测】纳斯达克100指数周跌幅达10.4%。
【各方立场与态度】市场关注点聚焦AI产业投资回报率预期的重新定价。
core_facts_en: [Core Event] Nasdaq 100 constituent stocks (including NVIDIA and Anthropic): 5.6% daily decline and 10.4% cumulative weekly loss
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Correction of investor expectations for AI ROI and valuation concerns
[Key Metrics] 10.4% cumulative weekly decline for the index.
[Key Position & Outlook] Market focus shifts to re-evaluating the ROI of AI capital expenditures.
headline_item.industry_impact_zh: 此轮科技股暴跌标志着市场已从单纯的“技术叙事驱动”转向“财务约束验证期”，资本支出强度与边际产出的剪刀差已成为市场审视AI资产的核心逻辑。随着英伟达等核心算力龙头的估值回归，AI基础设施市场的博弈点将从模型参数规模竞争转向推理成本的边际经济性与垂直应用场景的商业闭环能力。
headline_item.industry_impact_en: This sell-off signals a transition from narrative-driven optimism to financial validation, where the gap between CAPEX intensity and marginal output becomes the primary metric. With key incumbents facing valuation pressure, market focus will shift from parameter-count arms races to the economic viability of AI inference and the speed of commercial closure in vertical enterprise software.

headlines.title_zh: Wonder秘密提交IPO申请，拟整合外卖与食品科技
headlines.title_en: Wonder Explores Sale of Food-Delivery Business Grubhub
headlines.event_summary_zh: 食品科技初创公司Wonder已秘密提交IPO申请，公司此前通过收购Grubhub等资产，估值已达90亿美元
headlines.event_summary_en: Food technology firm Wonder, founded by Marc Lore, has confidentially filed for an IPO. Having acquired assets including Grubhub and Blue Apron, the company operates a vertically integrated model featuring automated food preparation and a diverse multi-brand delivery platform, with AI-driven menu development and an estimated valuation of $9 billion.
core_facts_zh: 【核心事件】Wonder创始人Marc Lore在美国资本市场：秘密提交IPO申请，此前通过并购Grubhub等强化业务闭环
【起因与机理】转型食品科技平台，利用AI与自动化技术提高交付与生产效率
【关键数据与实测】Wonder秘密提交IPO申请，此前估值达90亿美元。
【各方立场与态度】引入AI技术缩短餐饮品牌开发周期，深化自动化配送布局。
core_facts_en: [Core Event] Founder Marc Lore (US Capital Markets): Confidential IPO filing following strategic acquisitions including Grubhub
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Scaling food-tech operations via vertical integration, automation, and AI-driven brand development
[Key Metrics] Confidential IPO filing with a previous valuation of $9 billion.
[Key Position & Outlook] Integration of AI-driven brand development and robotic kitchen automation.
headlines.industry_impact_zh: Wonder的模式意在打破传统第三方外卖平台仅作为“流量中介”的局限，通过垂直整合供应端与自动化物流实现单位经济效益的优化。在当前竞争激烈的配送赛道中，Wonder的IPO核心叙事在于其不仅是餐饮配送平台，而是具备软硬件闭环的食品工业化与自动化零售平台。
headlines.industry_impact_en: Wonder’s strategy aims to transcend the limitations of traditional third-party delivery aggregators by vertically integrating the supply side and deploying automated logistics to optimize unit economics. Its IPO narrative hinges on positioning the company as an industrial-scale food automation platform rather than a mere delivery middleman.

headlines.title_zh: Databricks完成50亿美元融资，估值达1900亿美元
headlines.title_en: Databricks In Early Talks To Raise Funds At $225 Billion Valuation
headlines.event_summary_zh: Databricks首席执行官Ali Ghodsi宣布完成50亿美元融资，公司估值升至1900亿美元，年化经常性收入达70亿美元
headlines.event_summary_en: Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi confirmed a $5 billion funding round led by Coatue, with participation from Blackstone, MGX, and Sixth Street Growth, pushing the valuation to $190 billion. The company reports a $7 billion ARR with its cloud data warehouse contributing $1.5 billion at 100% year-over-year growth, alongside rapid monetization of its Lakebase agentic platform.
core_facts_zh: 【核心事件】Databricks首席执行官Ali Ghodsi；投资方包括Coatue、Blackstone、MGX、Sixth Street Growth在企业融资交易与数据分析软件市场：完成50亿美元融资，估值锁定为1900亿美元，年化经常性收入达70亿美元
【起因与机理】AI Agent市场爆发带动数据基础设施需求，投资者对高质量AI数据平台的竞逐加剧
【关键数据与实测】Databricks成功募集50亿美元，估值升至1900亿美元。
【各方立场与态度】融资受追捧主要源于Lakebase数据库及其AI Agent产品Genie的强劲表现。
core_facts_en: [Core Event] Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi; Investors: Coatue, Blackstone, MGX, Sixth Street Growth: Raised $5B at a $190B valuation with $7B ARR
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Surging demand for AI-ready data infrastructure and agentic workflows
[Key Metrics] Databricks secured $5B in funding with a $190B valuation.
[Key Position & Outlook] Investor appetite is driven by the performance of Lakebase and AI agent product Genie.
headlines.industry_impact_zh: Databricks的估值跃升标志着AI基础设施正从算力堆叠转向数据治理与Agent化工作流的深度整合。在云数据仓库领域与Snowflake的存量博弈中，其凭借高增长的AI Agent产品构建了差异化壁垒，这将迫使云原生数据库巨头必须加速向AI原生架构转型以维持议价能力。
headlines.industry_impact_en: Databricks' valuation surge signals a shift in AI infrastructure from raw compute to data governance and agentic workflows. By building a moat through its AI agent platform, it is intensifying pressure on cloud-native incumbents to pivot toward AI-native architectures to maintain competitive pricing power.

titans.name: Yann LeCun
titans.role_zh: Meta 首席AI科学家 / 深度学习三巨头 / 图灵奖得主
titans.event_context_zh:
纳偏差：它们比其他函数更喜欢生成某些函数。

正则化器只是强加了另一种偏差。

学习理论告诉你，你必须有归纳偏差，否则你无法通过合理数量的样本或试验学到任何东西（VC理论，没有免费的午餐定理）。

所以，从概念上、理论上、哲学上和实践上来说，正则化器都没有问题。
titans.event_context_en: @int_16h @torchedvision @MuzafferKal_ @mengyer @yingwww_ @choang333 @KuangYilun Regularizers are just a way to specify a
titans.quote_zh:
@int_16h @torchedvision @MuzafferKal_ @mengyer @yingwww_ @choang333 @KuangYilun 正则化器只是指定归纳偏差的一种方法。

您的模型架构和您使用的优化过程已经存在归纳偏差：它们比其他函数更喜欢生成某些函数。

正则化器只是强加了另一种偏差。

学习理论告诉你，你必须有归纳偏差，否则你无法通过合理数量的样本或试验学到任何东西（VC理论，没有免费的午餐定理）。

所以，从概念上、理论上、哲学上和实践上来说，正则化器都没有问题。
titans.quote_en:
@int_16h @torchedvision @MuzafferKal_ @mengyer @yingwww_ @choang333 @KuangYilun Regularizers are just a way to specify an inductive bias.

The architecture of your model, and the optimization procedure you use already have inductive biases: they like to produce certain functions more than others.

A regularizer merely imposes another bias.

Learning theory tells you that you have to have an inductive bias, otherwise you can't learn anything with a reasonable number of samples or trials (VC theory, no free lunch theorems).

So, conceptually, theoretically, philosophically, and practically, there is nothing wrong with regularizers.
